Fact.Name: Form 4835 line 7: gross farm rental income
Fact.Description:
Form 4835 Part I line 7, "Gross farm rental income. Add amounts in the right column for lines 1 through 6", rounded to whole dollars. Two arms:
1. the return claims a Form 4835 farm rental: the eight right-column legs added. 2. it does not: $0.
THE EIGHT LEGS ARE 1, 2b, 3b, 4a, 4c, 5b, 5d AND 6, and the dependency order below is the printed order so a reader can check the addition against the paper. The printed line names no members - it says only "lines 1 through 6" - so the set is derived from the form's own Specific Instructions, each of which cross references a Schedule F line whose summand status Schedule F line 9 prints inside its own parentheses. That chain is set out in full in this module's header comment.
NO FLOOR, deliberately. The printed line says "Add" and prints no "enter -0-" instruction, and line 6 can be negative because its instruction routes to Schedule F line 8, whose contents include the gain or loss on commodity futures contracts. So a farm rental whose only entry is a futures LOSS has a negative line 7, which the node test form4835/line-6-futures-loss-drives-gross-negative pins. This is the same call /scheduleFGrossIncome makes for Schedule F line 9.
THE GATE IS scheduleE:/claimsFarmRentalIncome, the population question Schedule E line 40 already asks, reused rather than duplicated. A return that has never entered a Form 4835 farm rental resolves Complete $0 here, which is what makes this module purely additive for the existing corpus. A return that stray-answers a leg without claiming the form also gets $0 - the gate is consulted first, and the node test form4835/legs-answered-without-claim-resolves-zero pins that verdict rather than leaving it latent.
WHAT CONSUMES IT, and it is no longer nothing. Two facts in this dictionary read this line, and both of them move dollars on the return: * Form 4835 line 32, the net, which is this line minus the Part II expense total on line 31. Part II ships, so /form4835Line32BeforeGate is a computed net, and it reaches Schedule E line 40 through /form4835Line40Amount whenever /form4835Line40Computed is true. This line therefore reaches Schedule E line 41, Schedule 1 line 5, total income and AGI. * /form4835Section175GrossIncomeFromFarming, which adds this line to scheduleF:/scheduleFGrossIncome to form the base the section 175(b) 25% conservation expense ceiling applies against, capping /form4835Line10 inside the same line 31 total.
TWO PRINTED CONSUMERS REMAIN UNWIRED, and each keeps its own filer attestation. * Schedule E line 42, whose first printed leg IS this line. The other two - a /formK1s box 14 code B field, and the Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) and Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) collections this dictionary does not model at all - remain, so line 42 keeps its whole-line filer attestation and nothing here reaches it. * The estimated-tax farmer/fisherman two-thirds test, whose Publication 505 numerator map names Form 4835 line 7 as an item beside Schedule F line 9. That test is not built.
THE DOUBLE SURFACE THIS CREATES, named rather than left for a successor to find. The graph holds a COMPUTED line 7 here and an ATTESTED line 32 net at scheduleE:/writableFarmRentalNet, and the attested net contains this figure inside it. No consistency check exists between them: the attestation is not retired, because it is the only source on a return that never opened Form 4835, and scheduleE:/farmRentalNetIncome chooses between the two on /form4835Line40Computed rather than reconciling them. A return that answers BOTH surfaces has the computed figure win, and the attested one is then dead weight the filer can still see.

Fact.Name: Gross income from farming for the section 175(b) 25% conservation expense limit (Form 4835 line 7 plus Schedule F line 9)
Fact.Description:
The base the section 175(b) 25% limit applies against: this farm rental's gross income (/form4835GrossFarmRentalIncome, Form 4835 line 7) plus the filer's Schedule F gross farm income (scheduleF:/scheduleFGrossIncome, Schedule F line 9). Form 4835 line 10's own instruction sends the filer to "the instructions for Schedule F (Form 1040), line 12" for the definition of the 25% test, and the Schedule F line 12 instructions state the base as "your gross income from farming (excluding certain gains from selling assets such as farm machinery and land)" — one combined concept for a filer who has both a farm rental and a farming trade or business, not the Form 4835 line 7 figure alone. Neither summand includes gains from selling farm assets (neither is built from a Form 4797 leg), so the exclusion the instruction names is already satisfied by construction and needs no separate term.
NOT FLOORED HERE, deliberately: both summands can be negative (a Form 4835 line 6 futures loss; a Schedule F accrual-method loss), and the signed SUM is what section 175(b)'s "gross income derived from farming" means. The cap, not this base, is where a non-positive result is floored to $0 — see /form4835Section175ConservationExpenseCap.
WHAT IS NOT IN THIS BASE, named rather than left to be discovered: the filer's share of gross farming income from a Schedule K-1 (Form 1065, 1120-S or 1041) and Form 4797 gains from the sale of draft, breeding, dairy or sporting livestock — both of which scheduleF:/scheduleFGrossIncome's own Description names as members of the broader "gross income from farming" concept used for the estimated-tax two-thirds test, and neither of which this dictionary computes. A filer with either has a broader true base than this fact supplies, so this fact can UNDERSTATE the section 175(b) ceiling for that filer; it never overstates it, since every summand it does include is a real leg of the same concept.

Fact.Name: Form 4835 line 10: the section 175(b) 25% ceiling on the conservation expense deduction
Fact.Description: 25% of /form4835Section175GrossIncomeFromFarming, floored at $0. Section 175(b)'s first sentence: "The amount deductible under subsection (a) for any taxable year shall not exceed 25 percent of the gross income derived from farming during the taxable year." Floored because the base can be negative (see that fact's own Description), and a negative ceiling would make a LesserOf(entry, ceiling) test return a negative number for a positive entry — not a printed possibility: a farm rental with no net farming income for the year gets no section 175 deduction, not a negative one.

Fact.Name: Section 175(b) shared conservation-expense ceiling remaining after Form 4835 line 10
Fact.Description: The taxpayer-level section 175(b) ceiling remaining for Schedule F line 12 after the allowed Form 4835 line 10 amount: the combined ceiling less /form4835Line10, floored at $0. Form 4835 applies the cap first because its existing line 10 computation is the first half of the shared-cap graph; Schedule F line 12 consumes only this remainder. Thus the two printed deductions together cannot exceed the one statutory ceiling.

Fact.Name: Form 4835 line 10 conservation expenses disallowed by the section 175(b) 25% ceiling
Fact.Description:
The part of the filer's line 10 entry the section 175(b) ceiling disallows for 2025: /writableForm4835Line10ConservationExpenses minus /form4835Section175ConservationExpenseCap, floored at $0. $0 whenever the entry is unanswered or at or under the ceiling, so this is complete safe.
OUTPUT ONLY, AND THE REASON IS THE ENGINE. Section 175(b)'s second sentence treats this excess as "deductible for succeeding taxable years in order of time", capped again each such year at 25% of that year's own gross income from farming — but this is a single year engine with no next year's return to carry it into, so the figure is REPORTED and not consumed. This is the same posture /form4835AtRiskSuspendedLoss already takes for its own section 465(a)(2) carryforward, which is why this fact carries an Export and no consumer.
THE CARRY-IN IS NOW BUILT, and this fact is its output: /form4835Section175CarryForward is the excess of the year total, carry-in included, over the ceiling. The prior-year intake is /writableForm4835Section175PriorYearCarryIn and the capped total is /form4835Section175ExpendituresIncludingCarryIn. What is still NOT built is the statute's ordering across more than one unabsorbed prior year: a single carry-in amount cannot say which year's excess it came from, and in order of time only matters once two years' excess compete for one ceiling.

Fact.Name: Form 4835 line 31: total farm rental expenses
Fact.Description:
Form 4835 Part II line 31, "Total expenses. Add lines 8 through 30g". THIRTY ONE summands, in printed order: 8 through 20 down the left column, then 21 through 30g down the right. Every summand is a complete safe line fact that resolves $0 when its writable is unanswered, so this line is Complete for any subset of answered legs.
THE LINE 30g FOOTNOTE NEEDS NO BRANCH, and that is derived rather than assumed. The instructions say "If you entered capitalized expenses on line 30g, your total expenses on line 31 will equal the total of lines 8 through 30f reduced by the amount on line 30g". That is a rule about PARENTHESES, not about arithmetic: line 30g is stored SIGNED here (a Dollar with no Min 0 fence, see /writableForm4835Line30gOtherExpensesG), so the printed mainline addition already produces total(8..30f) plus a negative capitalized amount, which is the figure the instruction describes. Fact.Name: Can this graph compute the Form 4835 figure Schedule E line 40 wants?
Fact.Description:
TRUE when Form 4835 Part I was answered (/form4835IncomeLinesAnswered) AND the figure the printed form routes to Schedule E line 40 exists in this graph: either the filer supplied the post limitation line 34c figure, which the printed line 34c says to "enter ... here and on Schedule E (Form 1040), line 40", or line 32 is income, in which case the form says "enter it here and on Schedule E (Form 1040), line 40". Lets scheduleE:/farmRentalNetIncome take both arms with a single predicate and keep scheduleE:/writableFarmRentalNet as its fallback.
THE 34c ANSWER IS CHECKED BEFORE LINE 32's SIGN, DELIBERATELY. /form4835Line32BeforeGate is the RAW difference and applies neither the section 465 at risk limitation nor a prior year's unallowed section 469 passive activity loss; the printed line 32 second bullet tells a filer who has a prior-year unallowed passive loss to apply it before entering net farm rental income, and if that leaves a net loss after applying it, to enter zero on line 32 and the net loss on line 34c. A filer who follows that instruction has an ANSWERED 34c on a return whose raw line 32 difference is still non-negative, so 34c is the more specific, filer-supplied figure and must be read before line 32's raw sign is: reading line 32's sign first would take the pre-PAL raw income and silently discard the 34c answer. Only when 34c is unanswered, or is answered with something that is not a loss, does line 32's own sign decide the arm.
THE 34c ARM ALSO REQUIRES AN ACTUAL LOSS, /form4835Line34cLossMagnitude above $0. Line 34c is by definition the DEDUCTIBLE LOSS, so a 34c entered as zero or as a positive figure is contradictory intake rather than the more specific answer this arm exists to prefer. The magnitude fact floors at $0 on exactly those entries and is complete safe on every return, so this fact stays complete on every return too, and a non-loss 34c is sent to line 32's own sign instead of displacing the computed line 32 and removing income from Schedule E line 40. On a return whose raw line 32 is a LOSS, a non-loss 34c leaves no arm to take: this fact is FALSE, and Schedule E line 40 keeps the attested scheduleE:/writableFarmRentalNet, which is the right answer, because the only figure the filer supplied for the loss contradicts the line it was entered on. When the filer records a Form 4835 loss and leaves 34c blank this fact is FALSE, so line 40 keeps the attested scheduleE:/writableFarmRentalNet, which that attestation's own prose says is already post limitation. Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: The Form 4835 amount Schedule E line 40 takes, both signs (line 32 income or line 34c loss)
Fact.Description:

THE 34c ARM IS CHECKED FIRST, for the reason /form4835Line40Computed's own Description states in full: line 32's raw difference applies neither the section 465 at risk limitation nor a prior year's unallowed section 469 passive loss, so a filer who followed the printed line 32 second bullet and entered a PAL-adjusted loss on 34c has an answer that must be read before line 32's own sign, not after it. It is checked first only for an ACTUAL LOSS: the arm also tests /form4835Line34cLossMagnitude above $0, so a 34c entered as zero or as income is contradictory intake, does not take this arm, and leaves the line 32 figure standing. The guard is /form4835Line40Computed and the two facts take their arms in the same order, so the amount is meaningful exactly when the guard is true.
THE LOSS ARM READS THE CAPPED FACT, not /writableForm4835Line34cDeductibleLoss directly. The capped fact passes that entry through unchanged unless box 34b is checked; when 34b IS checked, what reaches Schedule E line 40 is the loss capped at /writableForm4835AmountAtRisk and the excess leaves the form as /form4835AtRiskSuspendedLoss. /form4835Line40Computed still keys on the raw entry's completeness, because it is the entry, not the cap, that tells us whether the filer supplied a 34c figure at all.
WHY IT LIVES HERE AND NOT IN scheduleE. Both arms are Form 4835 quantities and the sign fork between them is a Form 4835 rule; putting it in this module leaves scheduleE: /farmRentalNetIncome a two arm Switch (this amount when /form4835Line40Computed, else the attested scheduleE:/writableFarmRentalNet) instead of a four arm one. scheduleE: /farmRentalNetIncome takes this amount behind /form4835Line40Computed and falls back to scheduleE:/writableFarmRentalNet on a return that never opened Form 4835, which is why that attestation is kept rather than retired. The Export stays because the consumer is in another module.

The project owner ruled SHAPE A, family wide. This intake is the fourth instance of the single amount convention and mirrors scheduleF:/writableScheduleFAmountAtRisk field for field; the line by line Part II build and the detailed Part III are not modelled here, exactly as they are not there.

THE INVERTED IsComplete GUARD, character for character the shape of scheduleF:/scheduleFAtRiskLimitationApplies and scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/atRiskLimitationApplies. COMPLETE SAFE ON EVERY RETURN: the IsComplete arm makes an unanswered 34c resolve $0, and the GreaterOf floor makes a 34c entered as income resolve $0 too, so the two facts that read this one can test "is there a loss here" with a plain comparison instead of a nested completeness guard. Fact.Name: Form 4835 line 34c after the section 465 cap: the deductible farm rental loss, signed
Fact.Description:
The line 34c figure Schedule E line 40 actually takes, SIGNED negative, after the section 465 at risk cap. Two arms, and each one's direction is stated because the sign is the whole point:
1. box 34b checked (/form4835AtRiskLimitationApplies) and line 34c is a LOSS: the loss capped at the amount at risk, entered NEGATIVE, zero minus LesserOf(/form4835Line34cLossMagnitude, /writableForm4835AmountAtRisk). The cap can only SHRINK the magnitude of a loss, never turn it into income; the excess it removes is /form4835AtRiskSuspendedLoss. 2. anything else, which is box 34a, an unanswered line 34, or a 34c that is not a loss: /writableForm4835Line34cDeductibleLoss unchanged, so every return already committed keeps the value it had.
INCOMPLETE, NOT UNCAPPED, when the filer checks 34b and leaves /writableForm4835AmountAtRisk blank: the first arm reads the amount raw, exactly as scheduleF:/scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss does. That is the family posture and it is deliberate. A silent $0 cap would disallow the whole loss and a silent pass through would grant a loss the filer has told us is limited; the return is simply not finished until the amount is supplied.
WHAT IS STILL NOT MODELLED, unchanged by this build: Form 8582. The printed 34c is the figure AFTER the passive activity limitation as well, and this dictionary builds no Form 8582 for the farm rental activity, so the filer's 34c entry is where that limitation enters. This fact adds the at risk cap on top of whatever the filer entered, which is the conservative order: the form tells a 34b filer to complete Form 6198 BEFORE Form 8582, so capping a post 8582 figure at the amount at risk can only reduce the deduction further, never restore one. Direction of the error: for a filer whose 8582 limitation already bit below the amount at risk this cap does nothing, and for a filer who entered the raw loss on 34c it now bites where before it did not.

Fact.Name: Farm rental loss disallowed by the section 465 at risk limitation, carried to 2026
Fact.Description:
The part of the Form 4835 line 34c loss the section 465 at risk limitation disallows for 2025: /form4835Line34cLossMagnitude minus /writableForm4835AmountAtRisk, floored at $0, and only on a return that answered Part I and checked box 34b. $0 on every other return, so this is complete safe wherever the amount at risk is answered.
OUTPUT ONLY, AND THE REASON IS THE ENGINE. Section 465(a)(2) treats the disallowed loss as a deduction allocable to the activity in the first succeeding taxable year, but this is a single year engine with no 2026 return to carry it into, so the figure is REPORTED and not consumed. It is the same posture scheduleE:/rentalAtRiskSuspendedLoss and scheduleE:/formK1s/*/atRiskSuspendedLoss already take for the identical quantity on their own activities, which is why this fact carries an Export and no consumer.
WHAT IT IS THE COMPLEMENT OF: /form4835Line34cDeductibleLossAfterAtRisk. The magnitude the filer entered on 34c splits in two, the part at risk (deducted this year, negative on Schedule E line 40) and this part (disallowed, carried). The two always sum to /form4835Line34cLossMagnitude, and the node fixture form4835/at-risk-cap-suspends-excess pins that identity.
THE 8582 ORDERING COMPRESSION IS NAMED HERE TOO: the filer's 34c entry is already post Form 8582 in the printed order, so a carryforward computed off it is a carryforward off a possibly already limited figure. Form 4835 itself sends a 34b filer to Form 6198 FIRST, so a filer who followed the printed order entered the at risk limited number on 34c and this fact resolves $0 for them. The figure is therefore a floor on the section 465 carryforward, never an overstatement of it. interpretation:provisional.
